title: Strieber writes to warn against the Oxford carbon dating of the shroud

tellings.quote: and I write Father Raldi a letter. Do not do this. They have to defend their paradigm. They will lie without knowing it. And they do bury that very thing. They say the shroud is from the middle ages. They destroy the research.

plain: In 1988, before Oxford scientists carbon dated the Shroud of Turin, the cloth many believe wrapped the body of Jesus, the writer Whitley Strieber says he wrote to a priest he names as Father Raldi telling him not to allow it. Strieber tells Michels he warned that the scientists "have to defend their paradigm" and "will lie without knowing it." He says that is what happened: they declared the shroud medieval and, in his words, "destroy the research," which would mean a real relic was written off by experts protecting their own assumptions.
